title: Holdout cohort canary with workload-aware signal weighting for pinned model upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: create a repeatable canary and A/B testing pattern that runs behind model pins and uses bounded holdout cohorts plus workload-aware signal weighting. This ticket scopes the PM-driven spec, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan so engineering can implement gating hooks in the pinning subsystem and Console UI.
acceptance_criteria: Canary mode that attaches a pinned model revision to a configurable holdout cohort (size 0.1%–10%) while leaving the primary pin untouched
Ability to assign per-cohort signal weights (e.g., size-weighted vs. workload-priority-weighted) for composite gating decisions
Rollout gating evaluates latency tail (p99), token-level cost, accuracy proxy via prompt-set snapshots, and failure rate within the cohort
Console exposes canary status, cohort composition, traffic split, and a single-click rollback for the pin
Telemetry pipeline emits cohort-level metrics and tagged traces for KV cache warmup and prefix-cache hit-rate
Documented playbook for rolling forward, annealing cohort sizes, and emergency rollback with clear thresholds
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec review with Eng and Design (this ticket) — finalize cohort syntax and UI hooks
Phase 1: Server-side API + routing: implement cohort selector and weighting primitives; unit + integration tests
Phase 2: Telemetry: add cohort tags to metrics, traces, and cost attribution; ensure Dashboard can filter by cohort
Phase 3: Console UI: canary creation flow attached to existing pin modal + visibility panel
Phase 4: Pilot: run 3 internal pilots (infra team, SE integration, two external beta customers) across diverse workloads
Phase 5: GA: open to all customers with default conservative thresholds and suggested prompt-sets
metrics_and_gates: Primary gates: p99 latency (<= baseline + 15%), token cost delta (<= +5%), error rate (<= baseline + 0.1%)
Quality signals: automated prompt-set evaluation (BLEU/ROUGE/F1 for structured tasks or model-specific eval scoring) with delta thresholds
Operational signals: KV cache warmup window < 5k requests, cache hit-rate degradation < 3%
Safety signals: content-filter violation events per 10k requests (no increase beyond historical variance), manual safety review flag
Composite decision: weighted score combining the above with configurable weights exposed in Console for power users
implementation_notes: Routing change must be compatible with cross-region fallbacks and with Dedicated pools — avoid global selectors that bypass capacity constraints
Add cohort id to request context and propagate to existing cost and latency attribution layers; update storage schema for cohort-tagged samples
Design: incorporate a lightweight cohort editor that lets PMs/SEs pin specific customer IDs or sample by workload type
Edge cases: requests that cross partition boundaries (e.g., multi-tenant accounts) should inherit the most conservative cohort assignment to avoid uneven exposure
Backstop: default to safety-first rollback if telemetry pipeline is degraded — don't continue canary without fresh metrics
Coordination: align with security/KMS team if cohort sample data will be stored for prompt-set snapshotting
